warning_texts: No check_plan rule covers a claim's population field or the prose of release/report.md (its title, population line and the closing sentence that country figures sum to the headline), so a relabelled population passes every machine gate and only this final review caught it.

gate_release_document's claims_rendered and caveats_rendered are listed under accepted_unproven in audit/check_plan.json because their proof run failed on a missing claim_register.json, so their 15 PASS checks were never shown able to fail, yet gate0_machine plan_proven reports 0 accepted unproven.

The five judgment auditors (gate0_semantic, gate_clean_auditor, gate_metrics_auditor, gate_claims_auditor, gate_release_auditor) left placeholder evidence notes, no artifacts and created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, and their 'independent' checks cite the registry under review rather than raw data, so t

All four worker results have placeholder summaries, created_at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (before the 2026-09-16 dispatch), no disclosures field and empty warnings, and each reports recomputing the refund rate as 0.473684, including worker_clean, which computes no rate, so these self-reports are not evide

The four carries are identical apart from their ids, are all dated 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, and define the population as status=delivered without the period bound, so a stage that trusted the definition alone would drop the 2025-01-01..2025-03-30 filter (net revenue would become 36741.51 with order O00

The spec period ends 2025-03-30, but the registry names it 2025-Q1 and clean_data/exclusions.json calls it the reported quarter, and Q1 ends 2025-03-31; no row is dated 2025-03-31 here, so net revenue stays 35741.52, but on a refreshed export this assumption would silently drop a day of revenue.

revenue_recognition net_of_refunds is applied by order date because the export has no refund date, so all 4493.50 EUR of refunds are netted inside the quarter; if any refund was issued after the quarter closed, the 35741.52 headline is understated by up to that amount.

CLM-REFUND-RATE counts a customer as refunded on any refund above zero, a rule written in check_plan.json rather than the spec; 15 of the 27 refunded customers had only partial refunds, so counting only full refunds gives 12/57 = 0.210526 instead of 0.473684, and no release caveat tells the reader p

The paying-customer basis is 2.50 times the order-row basis (0.473684 vs 33/174 = 0.189655), which matches risk_register.yaml's 'roughly 2.5x' but not the audit_spec comment's 'roughly a factor of three'.

In metrics/calculated_metrics.json, net_revenue carries numerator 40235.02 (the gross sum) and a null denominator, and the country metrics' formula text reads country = country; neither is rendered or checked, but a consumer who reads numerator as a ratio part would misread the headline.

The R04 row accounting (201 raw, 174 kept, 26 not delivered, 1 outside the period) and the R05 excuse appear only in analysis files and on neither release surface, so a report reader cannot see how many orders were dropped or that the lifetime-value question went unanswered.
summary: Every published number reproduces from raw_data/orders.csv: net revenue 35741.52 EUR over 174 delivered in-period rows, refund rate 27/57 = 0.473684 paying customers, PL 11181.67 + DE 11032.61 + CZ 13527.24 = headline, R04 accounting 201 = 174 + 26 + 1. All 21 rendered numbers on 3 surfaces are bound and exact, the machine release gate saw the same 21, and both reconciliations hold. One material blocker: the headline claim CLM-NET-REVENUE is registered with population 'all orders inside the period', and release/report.md shows the reader 'Population: all orders inside the period.' above figure
